/api/tools.name: insert_assets
/api/tools.description:
Register newly discovered assets in bulk; multiple types can be mixed in one call (see the type enum).
Required fields per type: root_domain->domain; ip->ip (must be IPv4/IPv6, not a hostname); subdomain->domain; app->app_name; service(HTTP)->url; service(non-HTTP)->service_name+port (at least one of ip/domain); endpoint->url+method. See each field's own description for the rest.
auth/technologies/params are append-merged, not overwritten.
Returns: {results:[{index,id,type}], errors:[{index,error}]}

assets.description: asset array; each element is one asset record

bound_domains.description: list of domains bound to this IP (optional for ip type)

company_id.description: owning company id (optional for app type)

content_length.description: HTTP response body size in bytes (optional)

domain.description: root domain or subdomain (required for root_domain/subdomain)

ip.description: IP address (must be IPv4/IPv6, not a hostname; required for ip type)

open_ports.description: list of open ports (optional for ip type)

record_type.description: DNS record type: A/AAAA/CNAME/MX etc. (optional for subdomain)

record_value.description: list of DNS record values (optional for subdomain)

service_name.description: service name, e.g. ssh/mysql/redis (required for non-HTTP service)

url.description: full URL including scheme and port (required for HTTP service)

/api/tools.name: list_assets
/api/tools.description:
Query the asset library: search by DSL expression, or fetch directly by id/ids; supports pagination.
DSL: field=value fuzzy (ILIKE) | field==value exact | field!=value exclusion | numeric fields support > >= < <= | a bare word = full-text fuzzy; combine with AND/OR (AND binds tighter), parentheses for grouping.
When neither id nor ids is passed, dsl must be non-empty.
Available fields: domain, root_domain, ip, url, page_title, icp, service_name, app_name, method, service_type, record_type, technology, port, status_code, company_id.

dsl.description: DSL query expression (must be non-empty when id/ids are not passed)

id.description: fetch by a single asset id

/api/tools.name: list_companies
/api/tools.description: List the companies in the asset library with their asset scopes and attributed asset counts. The optional search fuzzy-filters by company name (case-insensitive); empty returns all.

search.description: fuzzy filter by company name (optional, case-insensitive)

/api/tools.name: add_company_scope
/api/tools.description:
Add domains/IPs/CIDRs/ICP registrations/company keywords to a company's asset scope. Company names are unique: if the company doesn't exist it is created; if it exists it is reused.
This alone does not change what is in scope. Once the company is added to a task with add_task_scope kind=company, its domain, IP and CIDR lines are enforced as part of that task's scope; ICP and keyword lines are recorded for attribution only.
scope is one entry per line; the system auto-recognizes: root domain / URL / single IP / CIDR range / ICP registration / company keyword.
Always give reason explaining the attribution basis.

company.description: company name (created if absent, reused if present)

scope.description: asset scope, one entry per line

/api/tools.name: add_task_scope
/api/tools.description:
Add entries to this task's scope. Scope is enforced: insert_assets, the enrich tools, traffic_replay and capture_command_output refuse targets outside it, and check_scope tests a target against it. Targets are matched against root_domain, subdomain, ip and cidr entries and, for each company entry, the domain, IP and CIDR lines add_company_scope recorded for that company. A task with none of those allows every target, so the first one restricts the task to what is listed and later ones widen it. A company entry whose company has no domain, IP or CIDR lines allows nothing on its own rather than everything; add them with add_company_scope. Task scope is also the denominator of list_untested_assets, which counts a company entry's assets too. icp and keyword entries are not matched or counted; plugins receive every entry plus each company's scope lines.
Supported kinds: company / root_domain / subdomain / ip / cidr / icp / keyword.
Use the entries array for multiple entries.

kind.description: company / root_domain / subdomain / ip / cidr / icp / keyword

value.description: company name or id / domain / IP / CIDR / ICP / keyword

/api/tools.name: list_untested_assets
/api/tools.description:
Query the assets inside the scope of this task that haven't been covered by fact anchors yet.
Optional filter by asset type: root_domain/subdomain/service/app/endpoint/ip.
Pagination: page starts at 1, page_size defaults to 10. Returns {assets, total, page, page_size}.

/api/tools.name: graph_overview
/api/tools.description: The task board: goals and their states, open/running/done intents, recent facts, findings, credentials, coverage. Call this FIRST at the start of every planning cycle to understand what has been done, what is in progress, and what needs doing next. After subagents complete work, call it again to see their results and plan the next round. Includes strategic hints from the human/main agent that must be incorporated when generating intents.

/api/tools.name: add_intent
/api/tools.description:
Generate exploration directions into the frontier and link them into the exploration graph. An intent is an open exploration direction: describe freely in one summary sentence what to explore/verify/exploit.
Batch preferred: put multiple new directions into the intents array in a single submission (saves round trips). Returns an ids array, same length and order as intents. For a single intent, omit intents and pass the top-level summary.
After calling graph_overview and identifying gaps, use this to queue new work. Each intent is one exploration direction.

asset_ids.description: target asset ids this direction tests/attacks

intents.description: [Prefer this] array of exploration directions to add

parent_ids.description: upstream anchor ids: which confirmed fact/finding nodes this direction is synthesized from

summary.description: [single] one sentence describing this exploration direction

/api/tools.name: record_fact
/api/tools.description:
Write an exploration fact/conclusion into the exploration graph, linked to the intent that produced it (intent_id). Call this IMMEDIATELY when you learn something, do not wait until the end. Facts written here are visible to the coordinator and other subagents via graph_overview and list_facts.
Used to record both positive conclusions (fingerprinting/enumeration) and negative conclusions ('port closed'/'parameter not injectable').
Multiple observations from one exploration must be consolidated into ONE fact, not split into many.
facts is the preferred parameter: facts:[{...}] with one item per mutually distinct conclusion.
evidence = one line of key evidence supporting this conclusion.
confidence = observed (seen directly) | inferred (inferred from phenomena).
source = target_response | tool_output | third_party_intel | operator_input | inference (default).

facts.description: The facts to record, usually exactly one.

asset_ids.description: Asset IDs explicitly involved in this fact.

intent_id.description: The intent that produced this fact.

summary.description: Required: a non-empty one-sentence summary of this conclusion.

/api/tools.name: list_facts
/api/tools.description: Page through the exploration facts/conclusions, newest first (compact: id+summary+state+origin+source). All parameters optional: limit (default 20, max 100). Returns {facts, total}.

limit.description: number of entries to return, default 20, max 100

/api/tools.name: node_detail
/api/tools.description: Fetch the full content of an exploration graph node by id. Only for exploration node ids returned by list_facts/list_findings/graph_overview; for assets use list_assets.

/api/tools.name: add_hint
/api/tools.description:
Attach a strategic hint to the exploration graph; the planner reads it the next time it generates intents.
Batch preferred: put multiple hints in the hints array in a single submission. Returns an ids array. For a single hint, omit hints and pass the top-level text.

hints.description: [Prefer this] array of hints to add

/api/tools.name: set_goals
/api/tools.description:
Add exploration goals to this task. A goal = a final deliverable/verifiable result, not an attack step.
Batch preferred: put multiple goals in the goals array. For a single goal, pass the top-level text.
vulnclass is optional: the corresponding vulnerability class.

goals.description: [Prefer this] array of goals to add

/api/tools.name: set_constraints
/api/tools.description:
Add operation constraints to this task to bound exploration: type=allow (operations permitted) or deny (operations forbidden).
A constraint = a rule about which operations may/may not be performed.
Batch preferred: put multiple constraints in the constraints array. For a single constraint, pass top-level text/type.

constraints.description: [Prefer this] array of constraints to add

text.description: [single] the content of one operation constraint

type.description: allow or deny; defaults to deny when omitted

/api/tools.name: prove_goal
/api/tools.description: Call when you judge that a finding/fact proves a goal met: links the evidence node to the goal node and marks the goal met. A fact counts as evidence only when its confidence is observed. When evidence (findings or facts) proves a goal met, call this. When all goals are proved, the engagement is complete.

evidence_id.description: id of the finding/fact node that proves it

reason.description: why this evidence satisfies the goal

/api/tools.name: report_finding
/api/tools.description: Record a confirmed finding, with evidence providing verifiable proof such as command output and logs. Pass the current intent_id when in a task context. After reporting, the coordinator sees this in graph_overview and can use it as evidence for prove_goal.

/api/tools.name: list_findings
/api/tools.description: List the confirmed findings of this task (compact: id+vulnclass+severity+summary+state+status+traffic_count).

/api/tools.name: merge_findings
/api/tools.description: Merge two or more findings into a single primary finding. Evidence and assets from secondary findings are folded into the primary. Secondary findings are marked as duplicates with a pointer to the primary.

finding_ids.description: all finding ids to merge (must include primary_id)

primary_id.description: the finding to keep as the merged result

/api/tools.name: dismiss_finding
/api/tools.description: Mark a finding as dismissed (false positive). Dismissed findings are excluded from generate_report output.

reason.description: why this finding is a false positive

/api/tools.name: save_task_credential
/api/tools.description:
Record (or update) a test account for this task's target. ALWAYS call this immediately after registering an account on the target, with the exact username and password you chose. Same (domain, username) is overwritten in place, not duplicated.
Returns: {id, domain, username, source}.

domain.description: domain or host the account belongs to

password.description: the exact password that was set

/api/tools.name: list_task_credentials
/api/tools.description: List this task's test accounts: user-declared accounts plus accounts recorded by earlier runs. Check this BEFORE registering a new account, and use matching entries for authenticated testing.

/api/tools.name: record_coverage
/api/tools.description: Record what you examined on a surface for one risk class (use the goal's vulnclass as risk_area when it applies), including negative results, so an absent finding is never read as a clean target.

evidence.description: required for no_issue_found: a fact id, intent id or traffic id that shows the test

outcome.description: result for this surface and risk class

reason.description: required for ruled_out and not_applicable: why

risk_area.description: risk class, e.g. sqli, xss, idor

surface.description: what was examined: a URL, endpoint, parameter, host or feature

/api/tools.name: check_scope
/api/tools.description: Check whether a target (domain, IP, or URL) is within the engagement's scope rules.

target.description: domain, IP address, or URL to check

/api/tools.name: generate_report
/api/tools.description: Generate a Markdown penetration test report from the current engagement's findings, assets, and coverage.

/api/tools.name: create_engagement
/api/tools.description: Create a new pentest engagement (task + exploration graph).

description.description: detailed description of the engagement scope

/api/tools.name: list_engagements
/api/tools.description: List all pentest engagements with summary stats (goal, status, node/finding/asset counts).

/api/tools.name: engagement_status
/api/tools.description: Get the status of an engagement: goal, status, finding count, and coverage summary.

/api/tools.name: goal_met
/api/tools.description: Mark the entire engagement as complete. Call this when all goals have been proved and the engagement is finished. Sets the task status to done. Provide an optional summary of what was accomplished.

summary.description: optional summary of what was accomplished

/api/tools.name: update_engagement
/api/tools.description: Update the current engagement's goal or description.

/api/tools.name: delete_engagement
/api/tools.description: Delete an engagement and all its data (nodes, edges, findings, credentials, coverage, assets, constraints). This is irreversible. Both task_id and confirm=true are required.

confirm.description: must be true to confirm deletion

task_id.description: task id of the engagement to delete

/api/tools.name: engagement_activity
/api/tools.description: Show recent activity in the current engagement as a timeline of findings, assets, and graph nodes.

limit.description: maximum number of entries to return (default 20)

/api/tools.name: list_coverage_gaps
/api/tools.description: Identify testing gaps in the current engagement: assets never targeted by an intent, intents with no recorded facts, goals not yet proven, and service ports discovered but not enriched.

/api/tools.name: enrich_domain
/api/tools.description: Run DNS enrichment on a domain: resolves A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/NS/TXT records and performs reverse DNS on discovered IPs. Returns discovered facts and any new assets (IPs, subdomains from CNAMEs).

/api/tools.name: enrich_ip
/api/tools.description: Run reverse DNS on an IP address. Returns PTR records and any discovered hostnames as new assets.

/api/tools.name: enrich_service
/api/tools.description: Probe an HTTP(S) service for status code, redirect chain, server headers, page title, TLS certificate info (CN, SAN, issuer, expiry), and technology fingerprinting from headers and HTML meta tags. Scheme defaults to https for ports 443/8443, http otherwise.

scheme.description: http or https (auto-detected from port if omitted)

/api/tools.name: list_activity
/api/tools.description: List recent activity log entries for this engagement: intents started/completed, facts recorded, findings reported, tool calls. Optionally filter by node_id, kind, or since (time). Returns newest first.

kind.description: filter by activity kind (e.g. tool_use, tool_result, intent_start, intent_done, finding)

limit.description: number of entries to return, default 50, max 500

node_id.description: filter to activity on a specific exploration node

since.description: only return entries created after this time (RFC 3339 or duration like 1h, 30m)

/api/tools.name: log_activity
/api/tools.description: Record an activity log entry for this engagement. Use this to log significant actions, decisions, or observations that should be visible in the activity timeline.

action.description: what happened (used as the activity kind)

/api/tools.name: start_intent
/api/tools.description: Mark an open intent as running. Call this when you begin working on an intent.

/api/tools.name: complete_intent
/api/tools.description: Mark a running intent as done with a result summary. Call this when you have finished working on an intent and recorded all facts/findings.

/api/tools.name: cancel_intent
/api/tools.description: Cancel an intent that is no longer needed. Use this when an intent is redundant, no longer applicable, or was created in error.

reason.description: why this intent is being cancelled

/api/tools.name: export_engagement
/api/tools.description: Export the current engagement (or a specific one). Includes assets, exploration graph, findings, credentials, coverage, and scope. Format: json (default) returns the full export object; csv returns per-entity CSV tables (assets, findings, nodes).

task_id.description: task id to export (defaults to current engagement)

/api/tools.name: import_engagement
/api/tools.description: Import a previously exported engagement from JSON. Creates a new engagement with all the imported data (assets, graph, findings, credentials, coverage, scope). Returns the new task_id and exploration_id.

/api/tools.name: ingest_scanner_output
/api/tools.description: Parse output from common security scanners and import the results as assets and/or findings. Supported scanners: nmap (XML or greppable), nuclei (JSONL), httpx (JSONL), ffuf (JSON).

/api/tools.name: ingest_masscan
/api/tools.description: Parse masscan output (XML or JSON) and import discovered hosts and open ports as assets. Masscan produces nmap-compatible XML or its own JSON list format.

/api/tools.name: save_evidence
/api/tools.description: Save a piece of evidence (screenshot, PoC output, config extract, etc.) linked to a finding. Content is base64-encoded.

finding_id.description: finding to attach this evidence to

/api/tools.name: list_evidence
/api/tools.description: List evidence artifacts for the current engagement, optionally filtered by finding.

/api/tools.name: get_evidence
/api/tools.description: Read evidence content by ID. Returns base64-encoded data.

/api/tools.name: capture_command_output
/api/tools.description: Run a command and save its combined stdout+stderr as evidence (kind=poc_output). The command must only target in-scope hosts. Returns evidence ID, exit code, and an output preview.

finding_id.description: finding to attach this evidence to

/api/tools.name: traffic_search
/api/tools.description: Query the target traffic the recording proxy has captured (host is required; accepts a bare host, host:port, or full URL, optionally filtered further by URL substring or body keyword). When a port is specified, only that service's traffic is returned, avoiding cross-talk between different ports on the same IP. body_contains runs a full-text search over the captured request/response headers and bodies, supporting any substring including Chinese (at least 3 characters). Returns only an ultra-light index (id/method/url/status/resp_len) with no response content; once results are non-empty, use traffic_get to verify the request/response of each one, then hand the IDs that actually support the current vulnerability to bind_finding_traffic. Returns 3 by default, at most 10 per page; use page to paginate when there are more results.

host.description: target host (required): bare host, host:port, or full URL

/api/tools.name: traffic_get
/api/tools.description: Fetch the raw request/response of one captured traffic record by id (truncated when too large). Use together with traffic_search to avoid re-curling. A WebSocket (status 101) or SSE (text/event-stream) record shows only its handshake here; read its messages with traffic_messages. When proxy rewrite rules changed the exchange, the result starts with a REWRITTEN line naming the rule ids, and shows the request as the client sent it and the response as the target sent it. traffic_search searches only these original values: it never finds a value a rewrite rule wrote.

/api/tools.name: traffic_blob
/api/tools.description: Read a segment of an oversized request or response body by its blob hash (shown in traffic_get as @blob sha256:<hash>). Returns at most 8 KiB per call; use offset to page through.

hash.description: sha256 blob hash from traffic_get output

/api/tools.name: traffic_messages
/api/tools.description: List WebSocket or SSE messages of a captured stream exchange. Use after traffic_get shows status 101 (WebSocket) or text/event-stream (SSE).

direction.description: filter: c2s (client to server), s2c (server to client), or empty for both

/api/tools.name: traffic_replay
/api/tools.description: Replay a captured HTTP request (optionally with modifications). Fetches the original request from the given exchange id, applies any header or body overrides, sends it through the recording proxy, and returns the new response.

apply_rules.description: apply capture rewrite rules to the replay (default false)

modify_headers.description: header overrides: {name: value} to set, {name: ""} to remove

/api/tools.name: traffic_hosts
/api/tools.description: List all recorded target hosts with their exchange counts, most recent activity first.

/api/tools.name: traffic_har_export
/api/tools.description: Export captured traffic as a HAR 1.2 JSON document. Optionally filter by host.

host.description: host substring filter (optional; empty exports all)

status.description: status code or class filter, e.g. 200 or 4xx (optional)

/api/tools.name: traffic_stats
/api/tools.description: Aggregate statistics about all captured traffic: total exchanges, unique hosts, status code distribution, method distribution, top 10 hosts, time range, and average response size.

/api/tools.name: traffic_timeline
/api/tools.description: Show traffic activity over time for a host, bucketed by minute, hour (default), or day. Useful for spotting rate limiting, session expiry, and WAF patterns.

/api/tools.name: traffic_patterns
/api/tools.description: Identify traffic patterns: most-requested paths (by url_template), hosts with the most HTTP errors (4xx/5xx with status breakdown), and endpoints that appeared recently. Optionally filter by host.

host.description: host substring filter (optional; empty analyzes all traffic)

/api/tools.name: traffic_clear
/api/tools.description: Delete all captured traffic for a given host substring. Returns the number of deleted exchanges.

host.description: host substring to match for deletion

/api/tools.name: bind_finding_traffic
/api/tools.description: Link a traffic exchange (snapshot) to a finding as evidence. Use traffic_search to find the snapshot_id, then bind it here with a role describing how it supports the finding.

note.description: optional note about this traffic evidence

role.description: how this traffic supports the finding (default: supporting)

/api/agents.name: Pentest Lead
/api/agents.description: Orchestrates the engagement, tracks progress, and dispatches work to specialists
/api/agents.system_prompt: You are the lead pentester for this ARTEX engagement. When a conversation starts, call graph_overview to understand the current state, then ask the user which target or technique to focus on. Be direct and task-oriented: do not make small talk. Assess coverage, prioritize open intents, and dispatch focused work for them. Use the MCP tools to track assets, findings, and evidence, and prove goals when evidence exists. Stay within the engagement constraints at all times.

/api/agents.name: Recon Specialist
/api/agents.description: Reconnaissance, asset discovery, and port scanning
/api/agents.system_prompt: You are a reconnaissance specialist. Enumerate the target's attack surface: subdomains, hosts, open ports, services, and technologies. Record every discovery with insert_asset and keep notes on how it was found. Prefer passive techniques first, and stay within scope.

/api/agents.name: Web Tester
/api/agents.description: Web application testing: XSS, SQL injection, and authentication bypass
/api/agents.system_prompt: You are a web application security tester. Test discovered web surfaces for XSS, SQL injection, authentication and authorization bypass, and other OWASP Top 10 issues. Confirm each issue with a minimal proof of concept, capture evidence, and record findings with clear reproduction steps.

/api/llm/settings.global_system_prompt: You are an autonomous pentesting assistant driving an ARTEX engagement through ARTEX-CC. Use the MCP tools (graph_overview, insert_asset, insert_finding, etc.) to track assets, findings, and coverage. When a conversation starts, even with a greeting, orient to the engagement by calling graph_overview, then ask what target or technique to focus on. Be direct and task-focused, and skip small talk.
